study.title: Mini Drone-Based Precision Agriculture for Indonesian MSMEs: A Low-Cost AI-Assisted Monitoring System
study.short_title: Low-cost DJI Mini 2 SE monitoring system; YOLOX mAP 0.78 (11 cls)

segmentation.domain: low-cost AI monitoring system for Indonesian smallholder farms (MSMEs): U-Net semantic segmentation of rice-field zones, YOLOX instance segmentation and counting of fruit crops (tomato, mango, ginger), plus HSV-based leaf-health heuristics, on RGB drone video from a DJI Mini 2 SE via a mobile-to-YouTube-Live-to-Streamlit pipeline
models_tested: YOLOv5 pretrained (object detection for plant counting / disease patches)
segmentation.best_model: YOLOX instance segmentation: mAP 0.78 across 11 object classes (apple, banana, onion, tomato, mango, ginger, etc.); U-Net land-zone segmentation reported qualitatively only

dataset.name: Self-collected DJI Mini 2 SE RGB video over a 300 m2 vegetable plot + Roboflow 'recognition-agriculture' public dataset (training)
dataset.note: DJI Mini 2 SE (1/2.3-inch CMOS, 12 MP, f/2.8) flown ~5 min/session over a 300 m2 vegetable plot; phone-mounted live feed -> OBS Studio -> private YouTube Live -> Streamlit app; videos processed offline. Models trained on the publicly available Roboflow 'recognition-agriculture' dataset (11 classes incl. apple, banana, onion). Prototype-level validation; flight altitude/GSD not reported.

classes: and 5 further fruit/object classes (Roboflow recognition-agriculture, 11 total)
segmentation.backbone: YOLOX (instance segmentation, integrated with Streamlit); U-Net for land-zone semantic segmentation

mIoU.ambiguity: No semantic-segmentation metrics reported (U-Net rice-zone segmentation is demonstrated qualitatively).

PA.ambiguity: Abstract claims 'over 90% detection accuracy' but no metric formula or segmentation pixel accuracy is defined/reported.

crop_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 not reported; fruit classes segmented via instance segmentation (mAP-based).

edge.framework: Python Streamlit app, OBS Studio + private YouTube Live transport; processing offline on a standard laptop; pretrained YOLOv5 and YOLOX + U-Net

latency_ms.quote: The end-to-end latency from video capture to segmentation visualization in the Streamlit app remained under 6 seconds using a standard laptop.
latency_ms.section: IV. RESULT AND CONCLUSION / F. System Responsiveness
latency_ms.ambiguity: END-TO-END system latency (<6 s, video capture -> livestream -> Streamlit -> mask visualization) on a standard laptop, NOT single-inference model latency on an edge device. The model 'ran in real time with minor lag under dense object scenes'.

issues: System-prototype/demonstration paper with limited quantitative rigor: '>90% detection accuracy' claim in abstract lacks a defined metric; the only concrete number is YOLOX instance-segmentation mAP 0.78 (11 classes).
No quantitative semantic-segmentation results (U-Net rice-zone segmentation shown qualitatively); RQ1 semantic metrics therefore all unreported.
Latency <6 s is an end-to-end laptop pipeline figure, not edge inference; no on-device metrics.
Models trained on a generic Roboflow fruit dataset, not the local field; validation on a small 300 m2 plot.
